translated_text: June 21, 1940 My little wife, my darling, I'm quite close to you, but I don't know yet if I've found you. I hope I have a few hours' leave. If not, stay calm, my sweetie, even if you don't hear from me for a few weeks or months. Perhaps we'll go very far away. I don't know anything. If I have the opportunity to go there, to visit you at home, we'll talk about money. As for the situation, I'm in excellent health, and everything is going very well. Only outings with you. [illegible] If it becomes more dangerous, go (but only with the whole family) to Pezenas, you'll find friends there. But leave the address for everyone (in these cases) at Mrs. Morel's. Surely [illegible] I'll find the best thing for you and me, just please stay calm. It gives me much more strength. I haven't heard from you since Pezenas, but I hope everything is alright. I kiss you, my little one. You know how much I love you. Perhaps I think I'll tell you about it. I adore you. 1 Madame E. Zweigenthal at the Consul's. Correze 52. IN Zweigenthal I
